articles.title: Risk of Direct Russia-NATO Armed Conflict 'Extremely Low'
articles.description: The likelihood of a direct armed confrontation between Russia and NATO member states, including Estonia, remains extremely low despite provocative actions by the Baltic republics, according to Semen Boykov, deputy editor of the domestic and foreign policy department at the newspaper Izvestia. In a commentary provided to Pravda. Ru, the expert analyzed the causes of rising regional tension and assessed the risks of hybrid confrontation transitioning into an open phase. Previously, the Russian Foreign Ministry stated that Estonia and Russia are on the verge of starting an open war. Moscow accused Tallinn of attempting to organize a maritime blockade of Russia, providing its airspace for the transit of Ukrainian drones, and systematically persecuting Russian-speaking populations. Boykov noted that the Russian side's grievances are well-founded. The use of Baltic state territory and airspace for attacks on infrastructure deep within Russia poses a serious threat. He argued that Estonia, one of the most active supporters of the Kyiv regime, is deliberately escalating relations. Against the backdrop of the European Union's industrial decline and loss of competitiveness, small European countries are seeking ways to mobilize politically through the narrative of an external threat.
